why.title: Why PakkaQR codes never stop working
why.p1: Many free QR sites quietly create “dynamic” codes. The pattern you print doesn't contain your link — it contains their short link, which redirects to yours. When the free trial ends, they switch that redirect off and your printed menus, cards and posters stop working until you pay.
why.p2: PakkaQR makes static codes. Your link, WiFi password or contact details are stored inside the pattern itself. There is no middleman server, so there is nothing to switch off.
why.tradeoff: a static code can't be edited after printing. Tip: if you might change the destination later, point the code to a page you control and update that page instead.
why.checkLink: Check if your existing QR code will expire
why.articleLink: Static vs dynamic QR codes, explained

diagram.staticAlt: A static QR code leads straight to your website, with nothing in between.
diagram.staticCaption: The code holds your link. Scans go straight to you, forever.
diagram.dynamicAlt: A dynamic QR code goes through the vendor's server first; when the trial ends the server stops redirecting and the code breaks.
diagram.dynamicCaption: The code holds their link. When the trial ends, the redirect stops.

article.title: Static vs Dynamic QR Codes: Which Never Expire?
article.description: The difference between static and dynamic QR codes, why dynamic codes can stop working, and how to make codes that last forever.
article.h1: Static vs Dynamic QR Codes Explained
article.intro: Two QR codes can look the same and behave very differently. One holds your information directly and works forever. The other holds someone else's link — and can stop working the day a subscription ends.
article.blurb: Why some QR codes stop working.

sections.h: What is a static QR code?
p: A static QR code stores your content directly in its pattern: the web address, the WiFi password, the contact details. A phone reads it and acts on it with no other server involved.
Because nothing sits in the middle, a static code can't be switched off. It works as long as the thing it points to exists — your website, your UPI ID, your phone number.

sections.h: What is a dynamic QR code?
p: A dynamic QR code stores a short link owned by a QR company. When someone scans it, the company's server redirects them to your real destination.

That lets you change the destination later and count scans — but your printed codes now depend on that company. If the plan lapses, the trial ends, the company changes its prices or shuts down, the redirect stops and every printed code breaks.

sections.h: Why do so many “free” generators make dynamic codes?
p: Because it locks you in. Many sites make dynamic codes by default, let you print them, and then ask for payment once your menus, flyers and packaging are out in the world.

list: Use static codes for anything printed: menus, packaging, cards, signs, invitations.
Need to change the destination later? Point a static code to a page you own and update that page.
Need scan statistics? Use analytics on your own website instead of a QR company's redirect.

sections.h: How to check an existing code
p: Upload a photo of the code to our expiry checker. We read it and compare the address with a list of known dynamic-QR services and link shorteners — without visiting the link.

faq.q: Do static QR codes expire?
faq.a: No. There's no service behind them that can expire.

faq.q: Can I convert a dynamic code into a static one?
faq.a: Not the printed code itself. Open it while it still works, copy the final address and make a new static code with it.

faq.q: Can a static code be tracked?
faq.a: Not by itself. You can see visits in your own website's analytics.

about.title: About PakkaQR · Free, Open-Source QR Codes
about.description: PakkaQR is a free, open-source QR code generator. Codes never expire, nothing leaves your device, and there's no signup, tracking or watermark.
about.intro: Pakka (पक्का / پکا) means solid, guaranteed. PakkaQR makes QR codes that work — and keep working.
about.blurb: Why we built it and how it stays free.

p: Too many people print menus, cards and posters with a “free” QR code, only to find it stops working until they pay. PakkaQR fixes that by making static codes only: your data lives in the code, not on our server.
We also think a QR generator shouldn't need your email address, track you, or stamp a watermark on your logo.

list: Codes never expire — static codes only.
Nothing leaves your device — no uploads, no tracking, no cookies.
No signup, no watermark, no paywall, no limits.
Open source, so anyone can check these promises.

p: PakkaQR is a static website with no servers to run, so it costs very little. If it helped you, you can star the project on GitHub or support it with a small donation. There are no ads.
New QR types, translations, presets, frames and redirect-domain entries are all welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md in the repository.

privacy.title: Privacy · PakkaQR
privacy.description: PakkaQR's privacy promise in plain language: nothing you type or upload leaves your device. No cookies, no analytics, no third-party requests.
privacy.intro: Short version: we don't collect anything. Your QR codes are made on your device and nothing you type or upload is sent to us or anyone else.
privacy.blurb: Nothing you type leaves your device.

sections.h: What happens to what I type?
p: Everything — links, WiFi passwords, contact details, CSV files, logos, photos of codes — is processed by your browser on your device. It is never sent over the internet.

sections.h: Do you use cookies or analytics?
p: No cookies, no analytics, no fingerprinting and no third-party scripts, fonts or CDNs. All files are served from this site.

sections.h: What is stored on my device?
list: Your last design (colors, style, logo) so it's there next time — never your content.
Saved designs, if you save any.
Your recent codes, only if you turn on history. It's off by default and you can clear it any time.

p: The scanner uses your camera only while it's on, only after you allow it, and video frames never leave your device.
We never open or check links on your behalf. The expiry checker compares addresses with a built-in list instead of visiting them.
The site is plain static files. Like any website, the hosting provider may keep basic server logs (such as IP addresses) for security. Those logs never contain anything you type into PakkaQR.
PakkaQR is open source. You can read the code, or open your browser's developer tools and watch the Network tab: generating a code makes no requests.

faq.title: QR Code FAQ · PakkaQR
faq.description: Answers about free QR codes that never expire: static vs dynamic, printing sizes, logos, WiFi, UPI, privacy and more.
faq.intro: Everything people usually ask about PakkaQR and QR codes in general.

faq.q: Do these QR codes really never expire?
faq.a: Yes. The data is stored inside the code itself. Nothing depends on our website — even if PakkaQR disappeared, your code would keep working.

faq.q: Is it really free?
faq.a: Yes, completely. No trial, no limits, no watermark, no signup.

faq.q: Do you see or store what I type?
faq.a: No. Everything happens in your browser. Nothing is uploaded. You can check the open-source code.

faq.q: Can I edit a code after printing?
faq.a: No — that's the trade-off of a code that never expires. Point it to a page you control if you need flexibility.

faq.q: Can I track how many people scanned it?
faq.a: Not with a static code. Tracking requires a redirect server, which is exactly what makes other codes expire.

faq.q: Can I use the codes commercially?
faq.a: Yes, for anything. No attribution needed.

faq.q: How do I check if my existing QR code will expire?
faq.a: Use our free expiry checker — upload a photo of the code.

faq.q: Which format should I download for printing?
faq.a: SVG for printing at any size; PNG at 2048 px or more is also fine.

faq.q: What's the smallest size I can print?
faq.a: About 2 cm for a short link. Denser codes need more space; we show a minimum print size when a code gets dense.

faq.q: Why does my code say “might be hard to scan”?
faq.a: Common reasons are low contrast, a large logo, a narrow white border or a lot of data. Each warning has a “Fix it” button.

faq.q: Which formats can I download?
faq.a: PNG (256 to 4096 px), SVG, PDF, JPEG and WebP. You can also copy the image or share it on mobile.

faq.q: Does PakkaQR work offline?
faq.a: Yes. After your first visit you can install it as an app, and it works without internet.

faq.q: Is PakkaQR affiliated with NPCI or DENSO WAVE?
faq.a: No. QR Code is a registered trademark of DENSO WAVE INCORPORATED and UPI is a trademark of NPCI.
